## Monorepos

One run at the top of a monorepo gates every project the change touches, each with its own preset, and combines the results into one summary, one SARIF file, one JUnit file and one exit code. See [Monorepos](https://github.com/jhonDoe15/nitpicker/blob/main/docs/usage.md#monorepos).

- A repository is a monorepo only when its top `nitpicker.config.json` lists `projects` or it declares a workspace (npm, Yarn or Bun `workspaces`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, uv `[tool.uv.workspace]`). Every other repository runs as before; nested Python, Gradle or Maven folders get one stderr line that shows the `projects` list to gate them.
- The top `nitpicker.config.json` stays in force for every project: its settings are the base layer of each project's config, with its paths taken from the top, so an existing workspace keeps its `exclude`, `exceptions` and thresholds. Members whose dependencies are installed at the workspace root run as they are.
- Project configs can share settings with `"extends": "../nitpicker.shared.json"`. A loosening in the shared file is a `policy-loosened` finding in every project that uses it, and names the file.
- Taking a project out of `projects`, emptying the list, shrinking the workspace, moving a project to a folder no project covers or changing a project's preset in `projects` is a policy loosening. A base whose projects cannot be read fails the run with a tool error.
- `NITPICKER_ACCEPT_POLICY_CHANGE` takes several digests joined by commas.
- `--project <path>` runs the named projects. `--shard-count`, `aggregate` and `cache publish` are refused at the top of a monorepo with what to do instead; `"projects": []` keeps a repository one project.
